question: What will the Brent crude front-month futures settlement price be on September 30, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Anchor is the martingale prior: an individual futures contract's settlement 7 trading sessions out is best centered on its own current price (~$101.2 for Nov-26), not on the backwardated curve or on analyst 2H26 averages (EIA ~$90, BofA ~$83) which describe months, not this contract. Reference class is short-horizon front-month Brent changes in a high-volatility geopolitical-premium regime; the 2026 crisis-regime base rate gives a ~0 median drift with ~6.5% SD over 7 sessions. Adjustments: (1) Barchart CB*0 on 09/30 may roll to Dec-26, which trades ~$4 below Nov-26 in steep backwardation — I put ~20-25% on that print, shifting the center down ~$0.5 and fattening the left tail; (2) two-sided catalysts inside the window — UNGA Iran diplomacy and G7 emergency-stock-release talk on the downside (a credible ceasefire could unwind a large part of a ~$30+ risk premium fast), Saudi zero October allocations to European refiners, six-week pipeline repair estimates and further strikes on the upside. These roughly offset, so I keep the median at the spot anchor less the roll drag. Evidence is reasonably rich but fast-moving and the Sept 21 settlement itself was not yet known at forecast time.

Over 7 remaining ICE sessions the reference class of 7-day-ahead front-month changes in this regime implies ~8-9% dispersion, so the distribution is wide but centered near spot. I shade the median marginally below spot for three reasons: (1) an identified downside catalyst window - Pezeshkian at the UNGA Sep 23, Trump open to a meeting - and this market has repeatedly shed 7-10% in days on de-escalation headlines (Aug 1 cancelled strike, Aug 10 Bessent 'deal soon', April ceasefire); (2) Julius Baer calls the Saudi Petroline outage 'less significant than feared' and Saudi is offering more crude via Hormuz; (3) Sep 30 is Nov'26's expiry and the Dec'26 contract sits ~$4 lower, so there is roughly a 1-in-4 chance Barchart's CB*0 row for 09/30 prints the December contract. Offsetting: seven months of stalled diplomacy is the base rate (Iran's seven conditions unmet, Hormuz transits still ~4-8 vessels vs ~12-16 normal, Aramco cancelling October European cargoes), and escalation has repeatedly produced fast +6-7% weeks, giving a fat right tail. Net: median just above $100, right-skewed, with escape mass priced for a comprehensive deal (<$70) or an Abqaiq-scale strike (>$140). The thin Manifold market implies more upside than my mixture; I gave it modest weight given 14 holders and staleness.
